title: Quorum-driven upgrade orchestrator with autoscaler contracts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Upgrading dedicated GPU pools today either does coarse waves (which cause localized capacity dips) or fully serial rolls (slow). We need an orchestrator that vendors upgrades in quorum-driven waves and establishes explicit autoscaler contracts to guarantee capacity preservation during drains. Goal: build a controller that coordinates a quorum-based progression (wave approval when a percentage of tenants pass health checks), propagates short-lived upgrade leases to worker agents, negotiates autoscaler handoffs to reserve eviction budgets, and performs post-upgrade validations before advancing. This reduces SLA risk while improving upgrade velocity for LTS and minor releases.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can compute and enforce a quorum policy per pool (configurable percentage and min-hosts).
Worker agents accept time-limited upgrade leases and refuse new slot claims when lease indicates draining.
Autoscaler handshake API exists: controller can request a temporary eviction budget and receive deterministic confirmation or a negative response.
Upgrade waves only proceed when required quota of health checks and autoscaler confirmations succeed; otherwise controller gates progression and notifies ops.
Runbook automation triggers post-upgrade smoke tests and compares latency/cost baselines; failures automatically roll back or pause progression.
End-to-end tests simulate noisy tenants, preemption, and burst autoscaling with <5% SLA drift and logging for every decision point.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed for quorum policy model (fixed+percentage) and basic simulation harness; initial results: quorum of 30% with min-hosts=3 gives best tradeoff in synthetic workloads.
2025-02-20: Design review with PM and SRE; accepted autoscaler contract sketch (Reserve/Confirm/Release flow); added requirement for time-bounded leases to avoid stale-drain states.

2025-02-28: Prototype controller implemented (alpha) that issues leases and toggles node drain flag; integrated with local autoscaler mock; discovered race on simultaneous lease refresh — added optimistic token compare to worker agent.

2025-03-04: Canary test on non-production pool: wave size 10% progressed but stalled when autoscaler returned partial reserve; controller correctly paused and escalated; observed visibility gaps in console for per-tenant progress (tracked).
decisions: Use quorum policy combining percentage + absolute minimum hosts to avoid tiny-wave pathological cases.
Lease TTL will be short (default 2 minutes) with proactive refresh from controller to minimize stale state risk.
Autoscaler contract is explicit and synchronous: Reserve(eviction_budget) -> Confirm(token) | Deny(reason) -> Release(token).
Failure modes: controller will pause on autoscaler Deny and attempt backoff retries; after X retries will run a reduced-size canary if operator approval absent.
Integrate smoke tests as a gating check rather than manual sign-off to enable fully automated progression for low-risk minor releases.
next_steps: Finish autoscaler backend implementation and deploy to staging cluster (owner: Marco Ruiz).
Add controller endpoint to issue Reserve/Confirm/Release operations and wire to existing autoscaler RBAC (owner: Priya Nair).
Expand console telemetry: per-wave status, lease tokens, autoscaler responses, and per-tenant health signals (owner: Design/Console team).
Write e2e scenarios covering preemption, sudden demand spikes, and tenant islanding; target latency and error budgets documented in runbook (owner: QA).
Schedule SRE tabletop for rollout policy thresholds and escalation flow prior to production canary (owner: SRE lead).
